diagnosis: Repeated office or home blood pressure readings of 130/80 mmHg or higher are needed to confirm hypertension.
treatment: Lifestyle changes (DASH diet, exercise, weight loss, sodium reduction) plus antihypertensive medication when needed (e.g., ACE inhibitors, ARBs, calcium channel blockers, thiazide diuretics).
prevention: Regular aerobic exercise, weight control, limiting sodium to under 2,300 mg/day, limiting alcohol, and managing stress reduce risk.
when_to_see_doctor: Seek urgent care for blood pressure above 180/120 mmHg, especially with chest pain, shortness of breath, severe headache, or vision changes.

diagnosis: Fasting plasma glucose >= 126 mg/dL, A1C >= 6.5%, or 2-hour OGTT >= 200 mg/dL on two separate occasions.
treatment: Lifestyle modification (diet, exercise, weight loss) is first-line. Metformin is the typical first-line drug; other options include GLP-1 agonists, SGLT2 inhibitors, and insulin.
prevention: Maintain healthy weight, exercise at least 150 minutes per week, and eat a high-fiber, low-refined-carbohydrate diet.
when_to_see_doctor: See a clinician for persistent symptoms or for screening if you have risk factors. Seek emergency care for confusion, fruity breath, or vomiting (possible diabetic ketoacidosis).

diagnosis: Clinical diagnosis based on typical upper respiratory symptoms; testing is rarely needed.
treatment: Supportive care: rest, fluids, saline nasal sprays, acetaminophen or ibuprofen for fever or aches. Antibiotics do not help viral colds.
prevention: Hand washing, avoiding touching the face, and avoiding close contact with sick people.
when_to_see_doctor: Seek care for fever above 38.9 C lasting more than three days, shortness of breath, severe sinus pain, or symptoms lasting longer than ten days.

diagnosis: Clinical diagnosis based on characteristic symptoms; imaging is reserved for atypical features.
treatment: Acute: triptans, NSAIDs, antiemetics. Preventive: beta blockers, topiramate, CGRP antagonists. Trigger avoidance and a regular sleep schedule help.
prevention: Identify and avoid personal triggers, maintain consistent sleep, manage stress, and stay hydrated.
when_to_see_doctor: Seek emergency care for a sudden severe ('thunderclap') headache, headache with fever and stiff neck, or new headache after age 50.

risk_factors: vegetarian or vegan diet without iron sources
diagnosis: Complete blood count showing low hemoglobin, low MCV, low ferritin, and low transferrin saturation.
treatment: Oral iron supplementation (e.g., ferrous sulfate); IV iron or transfusion in severe cases. Treat the underlying cause of blood loss if present.
prevention: Iron-rich diet (lean meat, beans, lentils, fortified cereals, leafy greens) plus vitamin C to enhance absorption.
when_to_see_doctor: See a clinician for persistent fatigue, unexplained pallor, or pica (cravings for ice or non-food items).

diagnosis: Excessive worry on most days for at least six months, plus several physical symptoms, with significant impact on daily life (DSM-5 criteria).
treatment: Cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) is first-line. SSRIs and SNRIs are common medications. Short-term benzodiazepines are sometimes used cautiously.
prevention: Regular exercise, sleep hygiene, mindfulness, and limiting caffeine and alcohol may reduce symptom severity.
when_to_see_doctor: Seek help if anxiety interferes with work, relationships, or sleep. Call a crisis line for thoughts of self-harm.

diagnosis: Often clinical based on symptoms. Endoscopy or pH monitoring may be used in atypical or refractory cases.
treatment: Lifestyle changes (weight loss, elevating the head of the bed, avoiding triggers) plus PPIs or H2 blockers. Surgery for refractory disease.
prevention: Avoid trigger foods (spicy, fatty, citrus), eat smaller meals, do not lie down for 2-3 hours after eating, and maintain healthy weight.
when_to_see_doctor: Seek care for trouble swallowing, weight loss, vomiting blood, or symptoms not controlled by over-the-counter medication.

symptoms: dull or sharp lower back ache
diagnosis: Clinical assessment; imaging only for red-flag features (e.g., trauma, neurologic deficit, suspected infection or cancer).
treatment: Most acute back pain resolves within 4-6 weeks with activity as tolerated, NSAIDs, heat, and physical therapy. Surgery is rarely needed.
prevention: Core strengthening, proper lifting technique, ergonomic posture, and maintaining healthy weight.
when_to_see_doctor: Seek urgent care for back pain with leg weakness, numbness in the groin, loss of bladder or bowel control, fever, or recent significant trauma.

diagnosis: Serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D level below 20 ng/mL is generally considered deficient.
treatment: Vitamin D3 supplementation, dosing per clinician based on baseline level. Sun exposure of 10-30 minutes a few times per week helps.
prevention: Adequate sun exposure, fortified dairy, fatty fish, and supplementation when intake is insufficient.
when_to_see_doctor: Discuss testing if you have fatigue, bone pain, recurrent fractures, or risk factors.

diagnosis: Clinical: difficulty initiating or maintaining sleep at least three nights per week for at least three months, with daytime impact.
treatment: Cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia (CBT-I) is first-line. Short-term sleep aids (e.g., melatonin, low-dose doxepin) when needed.
prevention: Consistent sleep schedule, dark and cool bedroom, no screens before bed, no caffeine after noon, and regular exercise.
when_to_see_doctor: Seek help if insomnia persists more than a few weeks or affects daytime functioning, mood, or safety while driving.

risk_factors: family history of asthma or allergies
diagnosis: Spirometry showing reversible airflow obstruction, plus a compatible history.
treatment: Inhaled corticosteroids are the foundation; short-acting beta agonists (e.g., albuterol) for symptom relief. Avoidance of triggers.
prevention: Identify and avoid personal triggers (allergens, smoke, cold air); follow an action plan with a clinician.
when_to_see_doctor: Seek emergency care for severe shortness of breath, inability to speak in full sentences, or a peak flow below 50% of personal best.

diagnosis: Clinical, with optional skin or specific IgE testing to identify triggers.
treatment: Intranasal corticosteroids (e.g., fluticasone) are most effective; oral antihistamines (e.g., cetirizine, loratadine) help mild cases. Allergen immunotherapy for severe disease.
prevention: Reduce exposure: keep windows closed during high pollen counts, use HEPA filters, wash bedding in hot water weekly.
when_to_see_doctor: See a clinician if symptoms are not controlled with over-the-counter therapy or if they trigger asthma.

diagnosis: Clinical diagnosis during flu season; rapid antigen or PCR testing is sometimes used.
treatment: Rest, fluids, antipyretics. Antivirals (e.g., oseltamivir) within 48 hours can shorten illness in higher-risk patients.
prevention: Annual flu vaccination, hand hygiene, and avoiding close contact with sick people.
when_to_see_doctor: Seek urgent care for difficulty breathing, chest pain, persistent dizziness, severe weakness, or worsening of chronic conditions.

diagnosis: Urinalysis showing leukocyte esterase, nitrites, or pyuria; urine culture confirms.
treatment: Short course of antibiotics (e.g., nitrofurantoin, trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, fosfomycin) per local sensitivities.
prevention: Hydration, urinating after intercourse, and not delaying urination.
when_to_see_doctor: Seek care for back or flank pain, fever, vomiting, or blood in urine — these may indicate kidney infection.

diagnosis: Rapid strep antigen test, or throat culture for confirmation.
treatment: Penicillin or amoxicillin for 10 days; cephalosporins or azithromycin for penicillin-allergic patients.
prevention: Hand washing, covering coughs, and not sharing utensils.
when_to_see_doctor: Seek care for severe sore throat with fever or rash; antibiotics shorten illness and prevent rheumatic fever.

diagnosis: Clinical diagnosis based on symptoms lasting more than 10 days or worsening after initial improvement.
treatment: Most resolve with supportive care: saline nasal irrigation, decongestants, analgesics. Antibiotics only when bacterial infection is likely.
prevention: Manage allergies, avoid smoke, stay hydrated, and treat colds promptly.
when_to_see_doctor: See a clinician for symptoms over 10 days, severe pain, fever above 39 C, or vision changes.

diagnosis: Clinical, based on rash distribution, chronicity, and itch.
treatment: Daily moisturizers, topical corticosteroids during flares, topical calcineurin inhibitors, and trigger avoidance.
prevention: Frequent moisturizing, gentle cleansers, lukewarm showers, and avoiding known irritants.
when_to_see_doctor: Seek care for severe flares, signs of skin infection (oozing, yellow crust), or eczema unresponsive to OTC moisturizers.

diagnosis: Clinical, based on lesion type and distribution.
treatment: Topical retinoids, benzoyl peroxide, topical antibiotics for mild-moderate; oral antibiotics, hormonal therapy, or isotretinoin for severe.
prevention: Gentle cleansing twice daily, avoiding pore-clogging products, and not picking at lesions.
when_to_see_doctor: See a dermatologist for cystic acne, scarring, or acne resistant to over-the-counter therapy.

diagnosis: Elevated TSH with low free T4 confirms primary hypothyroidism.
treatment: Levothyroxine, dosed by weight and adjusted by TSH levels.
prevention: Adequate dietary iodine; no specific prevention for autoimmune cases.
when_to_see_doctor: See a clinician for persistent fatigue, weight gain, or cold intolerance, especially with risk factors.

diagnosis: Lipid panel showing elevated LDL, total cholesterol, or low HDL.
treatment: Lifestyle: heart-healthy diet, exercise, weight loss. Statins are the most effective LDL-lowering medications.
prevention: Diet low in saturated and trans fats, regular exercise, and not smoking.
when_to_see_doctor: Get screened periodically starting in your 20s-40s; sooner with family history.

diagnosis: Clinical, after ruling out red-flag features.
treatment: Acetaminophen or NSAIDs for episodic pain. Stress management, posture correction, physical therapy, and amitriptyline for chronic cases.
prevention: Regular exercise, hydration, sleep hygiene, ergonomic workstation, and stress reduction.
when_to_see_doctor: Seek care if headaches occur more than 15 days a month or change in character or severity.

symptoms: fewer than three bowel movements per week
diagnosis: Clinical based on Rome criteria; alarm features prompt further workup.
treatment: Increase dietary fiber to 25-30 g/day, hydration, exercise, and short-term use of osmotic laxatives (e.g., polyethylene glycol).
prevention: High-fiber diet, adequate fluid intake, regular physical activity, and not ignoring the urge to defecate.
when_to_see_doctor: Seek care for blood in stool, unintended weight loss, severe abdominal pain, or constipation lasting more than three weeks despite self-care.

diagnosis: In-lab polysomnography or home sleep apnea testing.
treatment: CPAP is first-line; weight loss, oral appliances, positional therapy, and surgery are alternatives.
prevention: Maintain healthy weight, avoid alcohol before bed, and treat nasal obstruction.
when_to_see_doctor: See a clinician for loud snoring with daytime sleepiness or witnessed pauses in breathing.

symptoms: cough lasting up to three weeks
diagnosis: Clinical; chest imaging only if pneumonia is suspected.
treatment: Supportive care: rest, fluids, cough suppressants. Antibiotics rarely indicated unless bacterial pneumonia is suspected.
prevention: Avoid smoking and second-hand smoke, hand hygiene, and influenza vaccination.
when_to_see_doctor: See a clinician for shortness of breath, fever above 38.9 C, blood in sputum, or cough lasting more than three weeks.

diagnosis: Clinical based on appearance and history.
treatment: Viral: supportive care, cool compresses. Bacterial: topical antibiotics. Allergic: topical antihistamines or mast cell stabilizers.
prevention: Hand washing, not sharing towels or eye makeup, proper contact lens hygiene.
when_to_see_doctor: Seek urgent care for severe pain, vision changes, photophobia, or symptoms in a contact lens wearer.
